Dated this the 21st day of May, 2020.

The revision petitioner is aggrieved by the conviction and sentence imposed on him by the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Kochi for the offence under Section 16 (1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50 (1) of the PFA Rules, as affirmed in appeal by the Additional Sessions Court, (Ad hoc-I), Ernakulam.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The revision petitioner was conducting an ice cream parlour in Chellanam Grama Panchayat.
On 7.12.1998, the Food Inspector, Kochi Circle conducted an inspection during the course of which, 1 litre of cow milk was purchased from the parlour, which, on analysis, was found to be adulterated.
The Food Inspector found that as on the date of inspection, the icecream parlour was being conducted without valid licence as mandated under the PFA Act and Rules.

Thereupon, a complaint was filed by the Food Inspector, arraying the petitioner as the first accused, the nominee of the milk manufacturing company as the second accused and the company as the third accused.
The offences alleged were under sections 2(ia) (a) (m), 7(iii), 17 r/w 16 (1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and Rule 50 (1) of the PFA Rules.

3. The trial court acquitted accused 2 and 3, finding them not guilty of the offences, while at the same time, finding the revision petitioner guilty of the offence under Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of the PFA Act and Rule 50(1) of the PFA Rules.
The appeal filed by the petitioner against the conviction and sentence having been dismissed, this revision petition is filed challenging the judgments of the trial and appellate courts.

4. Sri.Santhosh Subrahmanian, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner made elaborate and authoritative submissions on the various aspects of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the Rules thereunder, which now stands repealed and replaced by the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006.

Though attempt was made to assail the conviction contending that the provisions of the Panchayat Raj Act would come to the rescue of the revision petitioner, the learned counsel was fair enough to submit that the provisions of the PFA Act, which is a central legislation would prevail over the Kerala Panchayat Raj Act, a state enactment.

The contention was therefore essentially confined to the quantum of sentence imposed, which is simple imprisonment for three months.
5.

The penalty provision with respect to sale of article of food without licence falls under Section 16,
the relevant portion of which is extracted hereunder:-

2 (a) whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf, imports into India or manufactures for sales or stores, sells or distributes any article of food-- (i) which is adulterated within the meaning of sub-clause (m) of clause (ia) of section 2 or misbranded within the meaning of clause (ix) of that section or the sale of which is prohibited under any provision of this Act or any rule made thereunder or by an order of the Food (Health) Authority.
(ii) other than an article of food referred to in sub-clause (i), in contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or of any rule made thereunder;

sentences.text:
Reading of the provision shows that for offences under Section 17 (1) (a)(ii), with respect to the contravention of any rule made under clause (a) or (g) of Section 23 (1-A), the court may for any adequate and special reasons to be mentioned in the judgment impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine, which may extend to five hundred rupees.
But, if the offence under Section 17 (1) (a)(ii is not with respect to any rule made under clause (a) or (g) of Section 23 (1-A), the court may impose a sentence of imprisonment which shall not be less than three months, but which may extend to two years and with fine which shall not be less than five hundred rupees.
8.
Section 23 deals with the power of the Central Government to make Rules.
Sub-section (1-A) of Section 23 specifies the matters which the rules thus framed may provide for.
Sub clause(g) of Section 23(1- A) empowers the Government to frame rules defining the conditions of sale or conditions of licence of sale of any article of food.
Accordingly, Rule 50 of the PFA Rule has been framed.

As such, the offence of selling food articles without licence falls under the second proviso to Section 16(1) and is hence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five hundred rupees.

Considering the fact that the offence is of the year 1998 and the conduct of licence was for a short period only, as is evident from Exhibit D1, I deem it appropriate that the sentence of imprisonment be reduced to imprisonment till rising of the court.
In the result, the criminal revision petition is allowed in part by sustaining the conviction and modifying the sentence to imprisonment till rising of the court and fine of Rs.500/-.
The revision petitioner shall surrender before the trial court within two months to undergo the sentence.
